Posted May 2, 2002
Analysis By Richard Cowan

In February, I visited both Stockport, Greater Manchester, home of

Kevin, a very bright, likable fellow, is a fixture in Edinburgh's literary scene, and he is also drugs policy advisor to the Scottish Socialist Party. (Cannabis is probably the only thing we agree about!)

He had indicated that he was planning on opening a Dutch style coffee shop and had just returned from a visit to Haarlem, where

Now Kevin has made it official. Below is his announcement of his plans for the shop, which will be named for his publishing company, very appropriately, Rebel Inc.

This is enormously important for a number of reasons.

First, Kevin has too much standing in the Edinburgh community for this to be ignored, and quietly suppressed.

Secondly, Scotland has its own Parliament now, and the Scottish Executive admitted earlier this year that the drug war is a flop and they have to do something else. Scotland has a horrendous hard drug problem, and it would appear that a majority of the Scots support the legalization of cannabis. Although Scotland cannot completely legalize cannabis without London, it can " go Dutch " and redirect law enforcement.

Third, if this is done in Scotland, then the pressure on London to give up and do likewise will be overwhelming. Cannabis prohibition is crumbling in the UK, and this could be all that it takes to finish cannabis prohibition off in the near future.

Once Britain has gone Dutch, and it is too big and important to be pressured by DEAland, then the rest of the English speaking Commonwealth, meaning Canada, New Zealand and Australia, will have no excuse for not following suit. New Zealand and Canada already are leaning the right way.

The following is Kevin's announcement. Be sure and sign up for his newsletter!

In case you're wondering what's been happening since the last sighting of Rebel Inc... wonder no more... we've been gearing up (so to speak) for the opening in Edinburgh of Scotland's first Dutch-style cannabis coffeeshop. Read on ...

REBEL INC NEWSLETTER #1 - MAY DAY GREETINGS TO ONE & ALL

This Ain't Fiction

May Day Greetings to rebels everywhere. It was ten years ago this week (May 4th, 1992) that Rebel Inc magazine was first launched at an event in James Thins bookstore in Edinburgh.

It was an event that featured readings, from, among others, writer Irvine Welsh (in what was his first public appearance - over a year before Trainspotting was published).

Five groundbreaking Rebel Inc magazines later; plus over a hundred live Rebel Inc events all over the world; over sixty Rebel Inc book titles: we are now ready to unveil the third and most ambitious phase of the Rebel Inc project...

Phase One: Rebel Inc Magazine 1992-1995
Phase Two: Rebel Inc Books 1996-2001

Rebel Inc Cannabis Coffeeshop

This year, in the heart of historic Edinburgh, capital city of Scotland, we're gonna be opening the doors to our all-new Dutch-style cannabis coffeeshop. This revolutionary new
cultural café intends to challenge the current cannabis laws and provide a safe, stimulating and pleasant environment for lovers of freedom to gather, chat, plot and plan, listen to
nice sounds, and, of course, smoke your favourite herb.

The café will be the public front for the all-new Rebel Inc magazine (more details in the next newsletter) as well as the forthcoming Rebel Inc Books - a brand new and completely independent publishing house which has f*ck all to do with Canongate Books...

We're not going to say too much here but full details, Q&As, plus all the press, cuttings, etc., are now online at our brand spanky new website at

Word Is Virus - Spread It

On the first day of each month this newsletter will be keeping y'all bang up to date with developments with the coffeeshop, book publishing, and revamped magazine
projects, plus news on the campaigning front ...

If there's anyone else in your Outlook or Netscape address book who may be interested in the end of the war against drugs ... celebrating the legalisation of cannabis ... reading quality literature ... opposing miscarriages of justice, war, globalisation, and the surveillance society ... then please forward this email on to them ... thanks.

Your next Newsletter will arrive on June 1st, 2002

From all at Rebel Inc HQ:
Peace, Love, and, as always, FTM
